stop_condition: Stop when R2-F2, R2-F3 and R2-F4 are each adjudicated closed or still-open against this diff with a concrete failure path, and the qa-gate side of the ONE-validator question is answered: whether its accessors genuinely delegate or still parse structure themselves. Both directions of the R2-F3 clearing predicate must be checked together — an outside-the-unit change must NOT clear, a genuine same-unit amendment MUST. Scope is qa-gate.sh only.

findings.evidence: R2-F4 remains open. The waiver-disclosure branch calls `compute_design_conflict_open` only when `compute_design_satisfied` returns true. `cmd_design_conflict` does not require a satisfied verdict, so a valid artifact can receive an open U1 conflict while its verdict is missing, stale, or needs_revision. `approve --no-design` then skips the conflict reader and writes only the generic `[design bypass: ...]` marker at line 4951.
findings.description: A known open conflict can still be waived with a durable record indistinguishable from an ordinary no-design-phase bypass. The exact failure path is: create or amend a valid artifact, file U1's conflict before obtaining a satisfied current review, then approve with `--no-design`; the conflict-specific suffix is omitted.

findings.evidence: R2-F2 is closed only for approvals that reach `design-gate-precheck`: line 8420 now checks conflicts and returns nonzero. Every `--no-design` approval still carries the generic marker, however, and the new `[design conflict waived: units=...]` suffix is only additive. The Stop reader short-circuits on the generic marker and never consumes the new suffix. Thus an unconflicted satisfied design can be approved with `--no-design`, followed by a Beads-only U1 conflict that leaves the change-set hash unchanged; Stop skips the precheck and releases. Likewise, after waiving U1, a later U2 conflict is silently covered although the recorded unit list authorized only U1.
findings.description: The Stop-time path is not genuinely covered for bypass-bearing approvals, and the conflict-specific distinction is write-only rather than load-bearing on read. A conflict filed after approval can therefore remain releasable—the concrete R2-F2 failure class—and the R2-F4 unit-scoped disclosure cannot constrain later conflicts.

findings.evidence: R2-F3 is closed for both required directions. Each record is compared with `design_unit_content_hash` for its own `unit_id`: changing only U2 leaves U1's canonical hash equal and therefore open, while a genuine U1-object amendment produces a different hash and clears U1 once the whole artifact has a fresh satisfied review. The writer also compares an explicit `--design-hash` with the live artifact hash at line 10085, so stale caller values are rejected.
findings.description: The unit-specific clearing predicate and live-hash confirmation correct the two R2-F3 failure paths in this diff.

findings.evidence: The qa-gate side of the ONE-validator question is closed: `design_unit_json` delegates to `review-check.sh design-unit-json`, `design_declared_unit_ids` delegates to `validate-design`, and `design_unit_content_hash` hashes the delegated canonical result. qa-gate.sh parses only returned envelopes with jq; it contains no DESIGN-UNITS sentinel extraction in these accessors.
findings.description: The accessors genuinely delegate structural extraction and do not retain an independent artifact parser in qa-gate.sh.
